quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at other cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your hazard flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers right away. Move your car as far off the road as possible. Open your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by driving:

options.text: Through shallow water.
Faster.
Slower.
Through deep water.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Honk your horn.
Let oncoming cars go first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let oncoming cars and pedestrians go first. This is the law.

questions.question: Round signs warn drivers about:

options.text: No passing zones.
School zones.
Railroad crossings ahead.
Hospitals.

questions.explanation: Round signs warn you of railroad crossings. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: Children age ____ and younger must sit in the back seat.
questions.explanation: Children age 12 and younger must sit in the back seat. Use a child safety seat or seat belt.

questions.question: Stress can affect your driving by:

options.text: Reducing your ability to focus.
Lowering your chance of an accident.
Making you fall asleep.
Making you more aware of others.

questions.explanation: Stress and strong emotions make it hard to focus on driving. If you feel worried, angry, or upset, wait before driving.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill roads

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop. High speed crashes are also more severe.

questions.question: You can park in the access aisles next to handicap parking spaces.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Do not park in handicap access aisles. These spaces are for wheelchairs and wheelchair lifts.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
Good tires are not affected by water.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Slower speeds make roads more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Faster speeds make your tires less effective.
questions.explanation: When you drive fast on wet roads, your tires cannot wipe away the water. Your tires lose grip and you may hydroplane (slide on water).

questions.question: Driving at night requires more caution because:

options.text: Traffic moves faster.
There is more traffic.
You cannot see as well.
Accidents happen more often.

questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so you cannot see as far or as clearly. Use your headlights from sunset to sunrise.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?

options.text: Always, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road.
Only if the pedestrian signals the driver to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in the street, even if they cross against a red light or are not being careful.

questions.question: Increasing your vehicle's speed is the best way to avoid losing control on wet roads.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your tires can ride up on water and lose traction. This is called hydroplaning. The best way to prevent it is to slow down when driving in wet conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.
A railroad crossing is ahead.
A school zone is ahead.
Construction work is present.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, and emergency work.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.
Keep your speed constant on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down once you are on the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with siren and/or flashing lights approaches you?

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your four-way flashers.
Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and sirens approaches, immediately move to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Can you use parking lights instead of headlights when driving at night?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You cannot drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when visibility is low.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts raining while you are driving?

options.text: Drive faster than other traffic.
Drive at the maximum posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive closely behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain reduces visibility, slow down. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is too heavy to see clearly, pull onto the shoulder and stop until it passes.

questions.question: What are the most effective safety restraints in a traffic crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap and shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags used with safety belts provide extra protection in front-end crashes. Use both shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what must you do?

options.text: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and traffic crossing.
Slow down without stopping completely.
Stop completely and wait for a green light.
Slow down and check for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and look for pedestrians and traffic crossing.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign is a stop sign. You must stop completely. Look for pedestrians and traffic in the intersection. Wait until it is clear before you go.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the pavement onto the road shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed gently without hard braking. Turn carefully back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic as you return to the road.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back onto the pavement gradually.
Slam on your brakes and stop.
Gently brake to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to safely return to the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake to slow down. Then turn the steering wheel to safely return to the pavement.
questions.explanation: Keep the wheels on the shoulder. Gently apply the brakes to slow down. When you reach a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the pavement. Do not jerk the steering wheel sharply.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: When you turn left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just like you would yield to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. Go only when the intersection is clear of traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are stopped in a line of vehicles at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead pass through. There is no cross traffic. What do you do?

options.text: You may go through without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign before going.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign before going.
questions.explanation: You must make a complete stop at the stop sign. Look for approaching traffic before proceeding. Always stop, even if other vehicles are moving around you.
